evals.prompt: With rust-patterns loaded, add `parse_port_range(text: &str) -> Result<(u16, u16), PortError>` to src/lib.rs: it parses 'lo-hi' (e.g. '8000-8080') using `parse_port` for each end, and fails when either end is invalid or lo > hi (extend `PortError` as needed). The crate, its tests and Cargo.toml are in your working directory.
evals.expected_output: A scoped change that returns Result with the ? operator and a real error type (thiserror/anyhow), borrows rather than cloning, adds tests covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an Err case, and is clippy-clean and rustfmt-formatted (idiomatic, no needless clone, no unwrap()/expect() on the happy path).
assertions: Failure is returned as Result<_, E> using `?` and a real error type, not unwrap()/expect() or panic
Parameters borrow (&str/&[T]) rather than taking owned String/Vec or cloning to satisfy the borrow checker
Tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an Err case (table or rstest)
The code is clippy-clean on inspection (idiomatic iterators, no needless clone/borrow, no unwrap()/expect() on the happy path) and rustfmt-formatted
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted; no new unsafe without a documented invariant

evals.prompt: With rust-patterns loaded, add concurrent or async code that shares state across tasks.
evals.expected_output: Shared state behind Arc<Mutex<...>> (or a channel), no lock held across an .await, no blocking call on the async runtime, and deterministic tests; errors propagated as Result.
assertions: Shared state is guarded (Arc<Mutex<...>> or a channel); the design compiles under Send/Sync
No lock guard is held across an .await point and no blocking call runs on the async runtime
Tests are deterministic (no real network/clock) and cover an error path
No unwrap()/expect() on the concurrent path without a documented invariant
